newsitem.title: INDIA: Four India police candidates die in foot race.
newsitem.headline: Four India police candidates die in foot race.

text.p: Four Indian youths competing for jobs as police constables died in eastern India after running in an eight km (five mile) cross-country race in the midday heat, officials said on Monday.

State home (interior) secretary Sanjeev Hota told Reuters the four candidates died after completing the physical test on Saturday at Bhadrak, some 150 kms from Bhubaneswar, capital of the eastern state of Orissa.
Unofficial sources said a total of six youths had died.
Of the 10,000 unemployed youths who were candidates for the constable positions, some 450 were selected to take part in the gruelling cross-country race which began at noon.

Many candidates fainted after they finished the course, which took them through rice paddy fields. One collapsed on the course and the others died later, officials said. Nearly two dozen others were admitted to local hospitals.
The runners may have died from dehydration due to soaring temperatures, ranging from 35 to 40 degrees Celsius (95 to 104 degrees Fahrenheit), and high humidity, Hota said.
But he said doctors suspected food poisoning. During the race some candidates ate food at a roadside stall and drank water from fields contaminated with insecticides, he said.
Residents of the Bhadrak town staged a protest against the incident and demanded that the government take action against police officials who organised the race.
